audit.whatIsWrong: Keeper's Verdict is described only as a knockback that ruins your combo. Nothing says it is a channel, and nothing says Ki Burst cancels it.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Poppy channels a hammer strike that knocks enemies very far away', and the kit flags it as a channel - interruptible, any CC cancels it - as well as untargetable while it charges. Ki Burst is 11/10/9/8/7s of self-centred hard CC at 260 range. That means your 7-second stun cancels her 140-second ultimate outright, which is the single best trade available in the matchup and the page never mentions it. It also flips the level 6 instruction: the current advice is to hold Wind Slash until she has used R, when what you should hold is Ki Burst.
audit.corrected: Written into whys[4], the Level 6 spike, the mid prose, the late prose and wants.foe[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: Hammer Shock is called a knockup in whys[1], the early prose and wants.foe[1] - 'her Q knockup', 'while her Q knocks you up'.
audit.why: Riot's text for Hammer Shock: 'Poppy swings her hammer, dealing damage and creating a zone that will slow enemies and explode after a delay.' Damage, a slow zone and a delayed explosion - no knockup anywhere, and the kit flags carry slow and zone but not knockup. It matters because the two behave differently: a knockup is instantaneous and unavoidable once it lands, while a delayed detonation is something you can simply walk out of, and telling the player it is a knockup removes the response.
audit.corrected: All three fields rewritten to describe the slow zone and its delayed explosion.

audit.whatIsWrong: Steadfast Presence's cooldown is stated as 'roughly 14 seconds' in whys[3], the early prose, the first-item spike and wants.you[0] - the number the entire lane plan is built on.
audit.why: It is 20/18/16/14/12s. Fourteen seconds is only true at rank 4. At Level 2, when the page says the lane shifts hard against you, the real cooldown is twenty seconds - a window half again as long as the page claims, and the difference between one safe trade per wave and two.
audit.corrected: Real range written into whys[3], the early prose, the Level 2-3 spike, the first-item spike and wants.you[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Poppy, Poppy, Poppy, Poppy, Skill, Poppy, Poppy while the packet chart reads Skill, Poppy, Poppy, Poppy, Poppy, Poppy, Riven.
audit.why: The page's own whys say the same as the packet: whys[0] calls Level 1 'a skill-check farm-and-chip level' on a row marked Poppy, whys[4] says Level 6 is 'more her spike than yours' on a row marked Skill, and whys[6] says at two items Wind Slash 'ends her cleanly' on a row marked Poppy. Three rows contradict the prose beneath them. The poppy__riven mirror flipped exactly rows 0, 4 and 6 as one atomic group.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 4 and 6 flipped as one atomic paired group in both layers to Skill, Poppy, Poppy, Poppy, Poppy, Poppy, Riven, with ratings moved to match the mirror's inverse.

audit.why: The page's central claim is right and worth keeping: Broken Wings and Valor are both flagged as dashes, and Steadfast Presence stops enemy dashes around her, slowing and grounding whoever it catches. Riven really does lose her entire engage and escape to it, and the advice to bait it with a short Q1 rather than opening with the full commit is correct. I left that structure alone and only put real numbers on it.

edits.before: Steadfast Presence comes online and grounds your entire Q chain reactively — she can activate it the moment Q1 connects, leaving you auto-trading a tank with no mobility and her Q knockup incoming.
edits.after: Steadfast Presence grounds your entire Broken Wings chain reactively — she presses it the moment Q1 connects, leaving you auto-trading a tank while Hammer Shock's zone counts down under your feet.

edits.before: Her W cooldown is roughly 14 seconds at these levels, not long enough for you to reliably fish it out more than once per wave — she can play around it safely and out-sustain your damage with her passive shield.
edits.after: Steadfast Presence is 20s at rank 1 and only reaches 14s at rank 4, so the gap is wider than it looks — but she still plays around it safely and walks over her thrown buckler for a free shield.

edits.before: Keeper's Verdict gives her a knockback that can interrupt your Wind Slash cast mid-combo; she can press it the moment Blade of the Exile activates and reset the entire fight from range, making Level 6 more her spike than yours.
edits.after: Keeper's Verdict knocks you out of the fight and she is untargetable while it charges — but it is a channel, and Ki Burst cancels her 140-second ultimate outright, so hold the stun for that moment rather than opening with it.

edits.before: Poppy's W (Steadfast Presence) comes online and hard-counters every dash in your Q chain — she can proc it reactively the moment you press Q, so your all-in pattern is completely grounded until you bait it.
edits.after: Steadfast Presence comes online and hard-counters every dash you own — she procs it reactively the moment you press Q, but at rank 1 it is a 20-second cooldown, so baiting it out pays for a long time.

edits.before: Poppy's Keeper's Verdict (R) can knock you across the map mid-combo, erasing your Wind Slash execute window and turning your R into dead air if she presses it first.
edits.after: Keeper's Verdict (R) is a channel — Ki Burst cancels it flat, trading your 7-second stun for her 140-second ultimate, so never spend W before she starts it.

edits.before: Your Immortal Shieldbow spike is real but conditional — Poppy's W still has a 14-second cooldown, and if you bait it on a short trade then immediately re-engage, the shield and damage let you win the follow-up trade cleanly.
edits.after: Your Immortal Shieldbow spike is real but conditional — Steadfast Presence is 14 to 16 seconds by now, and if you bait it on a short trade then immediately re-engage, the shield and damage win the follow-up cleanly.

edits.before: At Level 1 you have no stun and she has no W yet, so it is a genuine skill check — Q-auto weave for chip but do not over-commit into her Q knockup with no escape. The moment she hits Level 2 and picks up Steadfast Presence, the lane shifts hard in her favour: every dash in your Q chain gets grounded on activation, leaving you standing still in melee range of a tank while her Q knocks you up. Respect the W completely — short Q1 prods to bait it out are your only tool, and the 14-second window after she uses it is the only moment a genuine trade is safe before Level 6.
edits.after: At Level 1 you have no stun and she has no W yet, so it is a genuine skill check — weave Broken Wings and autos for chip, but do not over-commit into Hammer Shock's delayed detonation with no escape. The moment she hits Level 2 and picks up Steadfast Presence, the lane shifts hard in her favour: every dash you own gets grounded on activation, leaving you standing still in melee range of a tank while the zone explodes under you. Respect it completely — short Q1 prods to bait it out are your only tool, and the 20 seconds after she spends it at rank 1 is the one window a real trade is safe before Level 6.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are still largely Poppy's lane — her W is up frequently, her E wall-stun punishes you hard if you Q toward terrain, and her passive shield means she absorbs more than you'd expect from short trades. The play is to track her W cooldown obsessively: when it is on CD, run your full Q-W stun-Q-E-Q pattern and cash the trade; when it is up, give nothing and farm. At Level 6 Poppy gets Keeper's Verdict which can launch you out of your own combo, so hold Wind Slash until you are already on top of her and she has used R — only then is the execute safe to release.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are still largely Poppy's lane — Steadfast Presence is up often, Heroic Charge wall-stuns you hard on its 10-14s if you dash toward terrain, and Iron Ambassador hands her a free shield every time she walks over her thrown buckler. Track her W obsessively: when it is down, run the full Broken Wings into Ki Burst pattern and cash the trade; when it is up, give nothing and farm. At Level 6 Keeper's Verdict can launch you out of your own combo, but it is a channel — hold Ki Burst for the instant she starts it, cancel a 140-second ultimate with a 7-second stun, then release Wind Slash.

edits.before: Two items in, the matchup finally tilts your way — your Shieldbow plus second item damage lets you burst through her passive shield and your Wind Slash execute does enough damage to actually kill her if she is below 40% HP. She has no escapes once her W is on cooldown, and your Q chain covers ground she cannot match without dashes. The danger is she will have stacked enough tank items that a one-sided all-in is off the table; play the pattern, not the ego — bait W, re-engage, and save Wind Slash for the execute rather than casting it early.
edits.after: Two items in, the matchup finally tilts your way — Shieldbow plus a second item bursts through her buckler shield, and Wind Slash does enough to actually kill her once she is low. With Steadfast Presence spent she has nothing that stops Broken Wings, and Heroic Charge only reaches 475 units. The danger is she will have stacked enough tank items that a one-sided all-in is off the table; play the pattern, not the ego — bait W, re-engage, hold Ki Burst for her ultimate, and save Wind Slash for the execute.

edits.after: Bait Steadfast Presence with a fake Q1 approach, then commit your real Broken Wings and Ki Burst combo inside its 12-20 second cooldown

edits.after: Hold Valor to shield Hammer Shock's detonation rather than spending it to gap-close while her W is still up

edits.after: Pin you to a wall with Heroic Charge for the stun, then detonate Hammer Shock into a free all-in while you are down

notes: Both packet suspectNames are FALSE POSITIVES: 'Pop Steadfast Presence' and 'Use Keeper's Verdict' are correct names with a verb in front of them. Unusually for this slice, the page's central claim is correct - Steadfast Presence really does shut off both of Riven's dashes - so I left the structure and put real numbers on it instead. The two genuine errors were the cooldown (20s at rank 1, not 'roughly 14' at every level, which understates the Level 2-3 trade window by six seconds) and Hammer Shock being called a knockup when it is a slow zone with a delayed explosion you can step out of. The best unstated fact is that Keeper's Verdict is a channel, so a 7-second Ki Burst cancels a 140-second ultimate - the page had it backwards, telling the player to hold Wind Slash instead. Full layer refers to Poppy as 'he' in tradeGood, tradeBad, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.late, dontsFull[0].d and report[2].t; those strings carry mojibake em-dashes so I left them for an encoding-safe pass.
